anomalies.observed: R10 (0 Ω) joins Net-(J9-Pin_3) to Net-(J5-Pin_3), so the two servo signal pins are shorted together. Both PWM GPIO paths are still present: R12 (1 kΩ) feeds J5.3 from /NET0036 (bus pins 19/21), and R22 (1 kΩ) feeds J9.3 from /NET0024 (bus pins 20/22). R3 (0 Ω) also ties J9.3 directly to the MAX3485 A line /NET0043.
anomalies.expected: The spec says R9–R12 are 0 Ω jumpers that select which M5Stack bus pin drives PWM1/PWM2 (ch.1 pins 19/21, ch.2 pins 20/22). R10 should therefore sit between a bus-side GPIO node and a channel, not directly between the two servo headers. In PWM mode the two channels must stay independent, and the serial shorts (R13/R14, here R3/R10) must be open.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2
PWM mode (populate R3/R4, and the appropriate R9–R12 pair for the Core variant; leave R13/R14 open)

anomalies.impact: The two servo signal lines are electrically joined. In PWM mode the two GPIO drivers (through R12 and R22) would fight each other, so channel 2 would not move independently. The 0 Ω link to the MAX3485 A line (R3) also loads the PWM signal, which can drive the GPIOs into contention and damage pins or servos.

parsed.summary: Most of the netlist matches the specification, including power paths, the MAX3485 wiring, the Q2/Q3 switching stages and the decoupling. The one clear deviation is R10, a 0 Ω link between the two servo signal nets, which the spec describes as a bus-pin selection jumper; as wired, it shorts the PWM channels together. Confidence is moderate because the spec's reference numbering does not match the netlist consistently.
